title: Second look at N-006: the label is beside the seven stars and is Bax's word, but its last glyph, its name and its referent are not settled
statement: I looked at the Yale scan myself (canvas 1006196): the whole right-hand wheel, the cluster crop cited in N-006, and the label alone at full resolution. What I can confirm from N-006: the upper-left segment holds one tight group of seven small stars with a curved line running from it toward the moon face; the word ZL gives as doaro stands immediately to the right of the group and is the label nearest to it; dchol,day sits under the single large star to the left; oalcheol runs under the curved line. I could also do what N-006 asked of a second look: I read Bax (2014) in the Internet Archive copy. On pp. 19-20 he writes of 'the VM word positioned to the right of the seven stars', a word of five signs whose first is 'shaped somewhat like the numeral 8', so his word is this label. I still dissent from confirming it as an anchor for the test, for three reasons. (1) The label's last glyph is not settled. The pinned transliterations split evenly: doaro in ZL 3b, IT 2a and the H and U lines of the interlinear file; doary in RF 1b, in GC 2a (8oay9) and in the V line of the interlinear file. On the scan the last glyph is a closed loop with a faint stroke curving down and left beneath it, so I cannot rule out either reading. An anchor is matched on its exact word, and this one differs in the glyph that carries the ending. (2) The published name is not Latin and is not independent. Bax reads the word as /taərn/ and warns against assuming 'the Latin TAURUS per se'; he credits the Taurus idea to Zandbergen's site (2004-2013), so the two sources for the name are one line of descent. N-006 lists only Latin names (pliades, pleiades, vergiliae, taurus); a reading in another language, which is what its one name source proposes, would be scored as a miss. (3) What the label names is not shown by the page. Seven small stars as the Pleiades is a conventional reading of the drawing (ZL page comment 'probably the Pleiades'; Bax; others), but nothing on the page says whether the word names the cluster, its constellation, a month, or something else, and the other star labels in this wheel have no proposed names to test the pattern against. A confirmed anchor constrains every future reading, so I would keep this one as a note, not as a constraint. It could be proposed again with both readings of the word declared and names in the candidate languages listed, and it would be stronger with a second labelled object in the same wheel.
